description: The new earthquake locations and focal mechanisms catalogues for the western Ionian Sea, Italy is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Tiziana Sgroi et al. The Ionian Sea hosts the last remnant of Tethyan oceanic lithosphere subducting beneath Calabria, where active deformation generates significant seismicity, including earthquakes exceeding magnitude 7. The main tectonic structures - the Ionian Fault system, the Alfeo–Etna Fault system, and the Malta Escarpment - accommodate African–Eurasian plate convergence and margin segmentation under a transtensional regime. Coverage: several countries (IT, MT); published in 2026. Formats: Excel. The data are held in INGV and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 0.7 MB. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is Open Access, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
